label: Manifest Destiny / U.S. westward expansion
description: Nineteenth-century ideology and political project that cast U.S. territorial expansion across the continent as destined or providential. It accompanied migration, war, annexation, settlement, resource extraction, state formation, and Indigenous dispossession, and later became part of the mythology through which the American West was narrated.

label: Nevada mining-boom frontier (1860s)
description: Specific Nevada manifestation of the nineteenth-century resource-extraction frontier: prospecting, mining speculation, rapidly growing settlements, territorial government, service economies, and boomtown journalism. It matters to Twain because he lived and worked within this particular case; the broader recurring pattern is represented separately.

label: Mark Twain — Roughing It
description: Semi-autobiographical travel and frontier narrative based on Twain's overland journey to Nevada, prospecting ventures, mining-boom experiences, newspaper work, and observations of the Far West.

label: American Civil War
description: Civil war from 1861 to 1865 over secession, slavery, federal union, and competing national futures. For Mark Twain it also ended his Mississippi steamboat career and preceded his move west with his brother.

label: Antebellum Mississippi River slavery society
description: The slaveholding social world of the pre-Civil-War Mississippi Valley, including river commerce, racial hierarchy, fugitive-slave law, towns, plantations, and vernacular cultures that form the historical setting of Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.

label: Mississippi steamboat culture
description: Commercial river world of pilots, boats, ports, navigation lore, regional speech, and mobility in which Samuel Clemens trained and worked before the Civil War. Unlike a one-person anecdote, this was a substantial occupational and regional culture with many participants and a reusable place in the graph.

label: Salinas settler-community formation (1850s)
description: Specific Salinas-area case of nineteenth-century western settler-community formation. Steinbeck's maternal grandfather Samuel Hamilton was among the early settlers of the area, and that family history became literary material in East of Eden.

label: Salinas agricultural & migrant-labor system
description: Specific regional case of large-scale commercial agriculture organized around grower-shippers, seasonal harvests, mobile farm labor, packing work, and sharp class and racial divisions. The broader recurring pattern of industrial agriculture and migrant labor is represented separately.

label: Steinbeck — East of Eden
description: Multigenerational Salinas Valley novel combining Steinbeck's Hamilton family history with the biblical Cain-and-Abel story, questions of inheritance, moral choice, family rivalry, and the making of California communities.

label: Steinbeck — Of Mice and Men
description: Great Depression novella about two itinerant ranch workers in California whose hopes for land, autonomy, friendship, and security collide with the precarity and hierarchy of migrant agricultural labor.
